name: Celestial Fragment
reason: The source concept of the 'fragment of Ying Tian' (the shattered former Heaven) was localized as 'Celestial Fragment', keeping the heavenly connotation while dropping the untranslatable proper name.
description: A fragment of Ying Tian, the shattered former Heaven, which Zane inherits around Ep 672. It can absorb the Heavenly Tribulation and has saved Zane's life; he keeps it secret alongside the soulforge in his mind and the Roaring Token.

name: Deadwood Gate
reason: The source term 'Withered Tree Gate/Withered Tree Door' was renamed 'Deadwood Gate' for a punchier Western fantasy register.
description: A whirlpool of shimmering silver light churning between two massive skeletal trees inside the Illusion Battlefield region, claimed by the Demon Night clan. It has a nasty reputation: the colossal trees animate and attack those who approach, and entrants leave half their points behind, but it is prized as a place to gather points.

name: Sorcerer Race
reason: The source term 'Ancient Sorcerer Race' was carried over directly as 'Sorcerer Race'.
description: A vanished ancient race whose relics and structures survive in the Illusion Battlefield region, some repurposed as shelters. Their systematic teachings disappeared with them, and artifacts like the giant divine tree trace back to their civilization.

name: Tessa
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Yuan Qingwei' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Tessa', a warm, grounded name fitting a principled young disciple. Her line about her father teaching her to repay kindness is adapted verbatim from the source.
description: A young female sect disciple (Eps 684-687) who shields the injured Zane from her own sect's killers despite being hopelessly outmatched; her technique is sloppy but her will is iron. She helps him out of a sense of repaying kindness, a value her father taught her, and keeps his secret afterward.

name: Elder Xander
reason: The source character Taoist Priest Qing Xu, Sect Master of the Void Spirit Sect, was localized as 'Elder Xander', a dignified Western name suiting an imposing sect patriarch; his Daoist priest framing was simplified to an elder title.
description: The imposing head of the Ethereal Spirit Sect (source Void Spirit Sect) and great-grandfather of the sect's young miss, whom he dotes on even as pressure mounts to marry her off before Maddox comes to collect her. During Maddox's campaign he anchors the sect's defenses, standing at the heart of a massive Runic Cipher while the arrays burn around him. The master sheet lists him enforcing discipline over Ethereal Spirit Sect disciples from Ep 487.

name: Darius
reason: No source counterpart is identifiable in the evidence; 'Darius' appears to be an adaptation-side name given to a lieutenant figure in Maddox's campaign arc.
description: A fighter who spent years in hiding until Maddox's plan to establish his own divine kingdom offered him a chance at revenge. He serves as Maddox's scout and messenger during the siege of the Ethereal Spirit Sect, relaying intelligence about destroyed teleportation arrays and executing field orders.

name: Life and Death Wind
reason: The source term 'Wind of Life and Death' was lightly reordered to 'Life and Death Wind' for smoother English flow.
description: An unnatural wind phenomenon that triggers a primal fear in all living things, appearing as bright yellow streams of volatile energy. Maddox unleashes it through his Nameless Saber during his campaign (Eps 749-937), though he can wield it without truly controlling it.

name: West Dragon River
reason: The source's English term 'West Dragon River' was retained unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A river in the Harlen Divine Kingdom and the site of a major tournament of divine geniuses from the four Divine Kingdoms, overseen by a white-haired priest. Zane fought there as a representative of the Crystal Martial House, and the battle and competition at the river are repeatedly referenced as a turning point in his Divine Kingdoms arc.

name: Nine Cauldron Martial House
reason: The source's English term 'Nine Cauldron Martial House' was retained unchanged.
description: A powerful martial house in the Divine Kingdoms arc with plenty of experts in both the Life-and-Death and Soul Sea Realms. Its most valuable asset is the Little Monster, a beast-raised prodigy the house discovered after its warriors trained in his forest; the standoff over recruiting him lasted months before the house caved to his terms.

name: Imperial Army
reason: The source's English term 'Imperial Army' was retained unchanged.
description: The Empire's military force, prominent in the early arcs (Eps 65-388). It fought a brutal battle against the Demons at Alba Imperia, counts nobles like the Sterlings among its advisors, and awarded Zane the Trinity Stones; striking one of its advisors invites the enmity of the entire Empire.

name: Skytop Peak
reason: The source's elite 'Tianyi Peak' ('Heaven One Peak') was localized as 'Skytop Peak', preserving the sense of the sect's number-one, sky-themed peak.
description: The reigning number-one peak among the Skyreach Sect's Thirty-Three Peaks, whose influence has grown in recent years. Its disciples enjoy lavish monthly allowances and their own sanctums, and it fields elites like Finn Donovan, Jeff, Shayna, and Wynn, dwarfing poorer peaks like Misty Peak in both recruits and resources.

name: Wynn
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xie Yun' was fully localized to 'Wynn', a short, punchy name for a blunt saber-wielding rival; his 'Asura Slash' technique was renamed 'Reaper's Chop'.
description: A Skytop Peak elite and heavy machete wielder known for his Reaper's Chop; when he first perfected the move he sliced a two-hundred-foot mountain clean in half with a single swing. In the tournament arc (Eps 258-305) his grey blade of saber light tears into Patrick's vortex defense, but Patrick's abilities prove to be in another league entirely.

name: Blue Phoenix
reason: The source's 'Qing Luan', a noble azure mythical bird, was localized as 'Blue Phoenix', swapping the obscure luan for the familiar phoenix while keeping the blue coloring.
description: A legendary beast ranked in the same class as the Roc and the Celestial Lynx, below the Greater Legendary Beasts. Tracy of the Skyreach Sect carries the Blue Phoenix bloodline and can burn its blood in battle.

name: Sea of Raging Fire
reason: The source term 'Burning Heaven Sea of Fire' was simplified to 'Sea of Raging Fire' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A major zone within the Cloud Road Trial (Eps 361-406): a vast lava sea dotted with stone pillars and platforms that serve as rest points. It is home to Red Fire Snakes and inferno rays, and its rising and receding lava tides dictate when trial-takers can advance.

name: Five Aging Processes
original_name: five decay of heaven and man
reason: The Buddhist-flavored source term 'Five Decay of Heaven and Man' was localized as 'Five Aging Processes', a plainer phrase for the end-of-lifespan decline of mighty cultivators.
description: The terminal decay that befalls even Supreme Lords who fail to ascend to True Godhood: once a cultivator's lifespan nears its end, they undergo the Five Aging Processes and wither away toward death. Some ancient powerhouses resort to soul-parasitism or sealing techniques to stave it off.

name: Emerald Task Force
reason: The source unit 'Green Mist Squad' was localized as 'Emerald Task Force', keeping the green color cue while sounding like a modern-register military unit.
description: Shane's military unit in the early war arc (Eps 63-79), fighting in disciplined formations of shields, spears, and arrows against the Razor swarm. The master sheet notes it is distinct from the Blackout Division; it suffered betrayal and heavy losses before Shane reorganized it to resume the hunt.

name: Landry
reason: No source counterpart is identifiable in the evidence; 'Landry' appears to be an adaptation-side name for a companion figure in the inheritance-trial arc.
description: A companion of Zane's during the inheritance-trial arc (Eps 1069-1112), prone to grumbling, sour commentary, and bursts of hysterical laughter when things go wrong. He is reactive and emotional, demanding explanations from Zane when events spiral beyond his understanding.

name: Snow Demon
reason: The source's English term 'Snow Demon' was retained unchanged.
description: An illusion-wielding demon encountered in the pyramid trial (Eps 1150-1152); each challenger faces their own Snow Demon. Zane's circles him and wears Elara's face to poison his mind with subtle illusions before he drives his hand through its chest.

name: Rowan
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Bai Wei' was fully localized to 'Rowan', a nature-flavored unisex name fitting a resolute Demon Night clanswoman; her scene vouching for the human protagonist at the gate is adapted directly from the source.
description: A Demon Night clan warrior (Eps 1244-1257) who welcomes Zane into her party for the Deadwood Gate expedition over her comrades' objections, declaring she will take responsibility if their lord objects. She leads from the front, heals the wounded, and keeps the group moving through the gate's attacks; her instincts about Zane's hidden strength prove accurate.

name: Dylan
reason: No source counterpart is identifiable in the evidence; 'Dylan' appears to be an adaptation-side name for a Sanctuary-affiliated companion of Olivia.
description: A Sanctuary-affiliated warrior in Olivia's circle (Eps 571-620) who initially sneers at Zane as a mere human War Fighter and poisons the well against him. After the Sanctuary orders the group to stay on good terms with Zane, Dylan must swallow his pride, visibly chafing at Zane's rise.

name: Reverse Spirit Channel
reason: The source's English term 'Reverse Spirit Channel' was retained unchanged.
description: A secret passage linking the Divine Kingdoms to the humans of the Upper World, maintained by a secret order that includes the Holy Maiden of the York Divine Kingdom. Every few years priceless treasures are sent down through it, and in wartime it carries messages and brings weapons, resources, and reinforcements from above.

name: Cliff
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Lin Geng' was fully localized to 'Cliff', a solid, rugged one-syllable name fitting a dependable senior disciple; his demon-slaying boast scene is adapted directly from the source.
description: A Misty Peak Varsity member and senior swordsman (Eps 111-233) who leads the team during the Demon Slaying Trial. He proudly recounts having slain a demon in his own outer-disciple days and confronts the demon that devoured a fellow disciple and wore his body. The master sheet's 'Bloodwood Cliff' sect is an unrelated entity.

name: Blackrock Peak
reason: The source term 'Black Rock Peak' was compounded to 'Blackrock Peak' for a cleaner English place name.
description: One of the top-tier peaks of the Skyreach Sect, known for its array specialists and generous disciple benefits. Its Varsity members swore blood oaths to shield the girls of Maiden's Peak and all ten died keeping that promise against the Demon Commanders; it is also home to Mack, a rival in the sect competition arc.

name: Apex Dragon
reason: The source's 'Five-Clawed Golden Dragon' summon was renamed 'Apex Dragon', trading the Chinese five-claw imperial symbolism for a Western shorthand for a top-tier dragon.
description: A five-clawed dragon summon wielded by an Imperial Army general in the White Emperor City arc (Eps 127-139), slithering like a colossal snake and savaging Zane's Shadow Dragon. Zane's enormous black dragon turns the tables by swallowing the Apex Dragons whole, tripling in size as it devours them.

name: Alba Imperia
reason: The source's 'White Emperor City' was localized as 'Alba Imperia', a Latinate coinage preserving both elements ('alba' = white, 'imperia' = imperial) with an epic ring.
description: A major city of the Empire (Eps 177-1017) and the site of the brutal battle between the Imperial Army and the Demons, after which the Sect's disciples were sent home - all except Zane. It is where Zane fought demon generals and stood up to House Sterling, feats that spread his reputation; the master sheet notes he explored it with Ethan, Ingrid, and friends.

name: House Brandt
reason: The source's 'Meng family of Wang Chuan' was localized as 'House Brandt' to fit the adaptation's Western noble-house naming; its long-standing feud with the Pei family became the tension with House Pauling.
description: A noble house based at Dragon's Keep (Eps 71-188), represented by Leo Brandt, a Nature Level fighter. Relations between House Brandt and House Pauling have long been tense, and the house weighs throwing its backing behind Zane if he can amass a million points and the strength to match.

name: Nicholas
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Yue Qi' was fully localized to 'Nicholas', a stately name fitting a composed, patient spear master; his mountain-steady bearing and spear drawn from his back are adapted from the source.
description: A Soul Realm disciple ranked seventy-second in the Skyreach Sect Rankings (Eps 247-249), famed for legendary patience: he absorbs pressure like stone absorbs rain until his restraint shatters and his pent-up rage sweeps the arena. He fights with a spear slid from his back, and his opponent dares to meet it with footwork alone.

name: Soul Harvesting Ritual
reason: The source's sexually-charged 'Great Demonic Joyous Union Array' pursued by the villain was renamed and sanitized as the 'Soul Harvesting Ritual', recasting it as a soul-based forbidden rite suitable for the adaptation's audience.
description: A forbidden ritual Maddox pursues to break the bonds of death, requiring three specific women who must first reach the Inner-Core Realm; Elara is among his targets, which drives the long pursuit of her across the mid-story arcs (Eps 308-757). Marilyn's loss leaves Maddox one woman short, buying Zane precious time. The master sheet introduces it at Ep 351 as the goal of the entity threatening Elara.

name: Cloud Road Trial
reason: The source's 'Road of Trials' (also rendered 'Trial Challenger's Road' / 'Path of the Trialtakers') was localized as 'Cloud Road Trial', tying the event to the Cloud Hall that hosts it.
description: A multi-stage trial dimension opened by the Cloud Hall for prospective disciples, testing weaponsmithing skill and combat across zones like the Sea of Raging Fire, cliff challenges, Hidden Tests, the Death Road, and the Thrilling Icy Plain. Zane was the most crucial disciple in its running (Eps 348-406), and entry is via a gateway powered by Supreme Vitality crystals; millions of students compete, and taking first place is a career-defining feat.
